transcript.text: Our Dyson (one of the V ones, purple bits) keeps cutting out after about 5-10 seconds. Not every time - some days it does a whole room fine. It's maybe 5 years old. Already cleaned the filter and checked for blockages. Battery or something else?

Intermittent cutting out after just a few seconds is most often caused by the motor overheating because airflow is restricted. Even if you've checked for blockages, a filter that isn't 100% dry or a partial clog in the wand can trigger this safety cut-out. On a 5-year-old cordless Dyson, a degrading battery is also possible, but we should rule out airflow and charging issues first. 1. Was it set to Boost/Max mode when it failed? This drains batteries very quickly and can cause overheating.
2. When you place it on the charger, does the light turn on? If not, wipe the metal contacts on both the vacuum body and the dock with a dry cloth.
[Helpful to see: image "Poor suction — what to check first" — A vacuum that pulses or cuts out after running is usually a full bin, a dirty filter or a blockage starving the airflow — check and clear those before suspecting battery, charger or motor. Switch off and unplug first. Typical layout — your model may differ.]
Yes, on Max it nearly always stops within a few seconds. Charger light comes on and the plug goes in properly. Filter was washed and dried for 48 hours too. Is it the battery then?

[Heading: Battery degradation limiting Max mode performance]
It is almost certainly the battery. On Dyson V-series models, Max mode draws so much current that a 5-year-old battery (which typically lasts 3-4 years before significant capacity loss) will hit its thermal protection limit within seconds and cut out to prevent overheating or damage. You should be able to use the vacuum on Normal mode for a reasonable time, as that draws less current and generates less heat. If you need full power, the only fix is to replace the battery unit. Dyson batteries are user-replaceable on most V-series models (usually sliding off the back of the handle). I recommend sourcing an official replacement or a high-quality third-party equivalent from a reputable retailer.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
The label under the bin says SV11. Before I spend £60+, is there anything else worth ruling out, or is it definitely the battery? I've got no spare battery to test with and no multimeter.

[Heading: Battery degradation in Max mode]
Switch it off and unplug it (or take the battery off) first. For the Dyson SV11 (V8 series), if it cuts out in Max mode but runs longer on Normal mode with a clean filter and clear airflow, it is almost certainly the battery. At 5 years old, the cells have likely lost significant capacity; when you demand high power (Max), the voltage drops rapidly, triggering the safety cut-out before the motor overheats from blockage. If it works fine on Normal but fails in Max, you can continue using it on Normal indefinitely, or replace the battery if you need full power.
